headline: Panasonic Holdings plans to build humanoid robots, with production targeted for 2029, according to an interview its chief AI officer gave Nikkei.
score_reason: Large manufacturer entering humanoids; only the opening of the article could be read and the timeline is a stated aim, so one point lower.
importance_line: Panasonic, a major Japanese maker of electronics and batteries, says it wants to build humanoid robots for factories and warehouses by 2029; this adds a large industrial player to the humanoid race, but the plan is a stated aim from one interview, and how the battery business fits in is not explained beyond the headline.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Panasonic Holdings, the Japanese electronics and battery group, plans to develop humanoid robots and aims to begin making them by 2029, citing an interview with its chief AI officer, Akira Sakakibara. The report says the machines are meant to work in factories and warehouses, and its headline ties the plan to Panasonic's battery business.
notes: Nikkei is paywalled: only the first paragraph and subhead were read, so verified_text is false although the summary stays within what was readable. No other outlet carried the story on Google News RSS.
